subtopics.title: The Nature and Measurement of Unemployment

questions.question: The strictly unemployed are working-age people who are:
options: Without work, AVAILABLE for work, and ACTIVELY SEEKING it

questions.question: Saying South African unemployment is STRUCTURAL rather than merely cyclical means:
options: It persists through upswings — so the business cycle alone cannot explain it

questions.question: Long-term unemployment makes re-entry harder because:
options: Employers are legally barred from hiring the long-term unemployed
It erodes skills, networks and confidence the longer it lasts

questions.question: Why will growth alone not clear South Africa's unemployment?
options: Growth that is capital-intensive or skill-concentrated can raise output while bypassing the unskilled

questions.question: FRICTIONAL unemployment describes:
options: People BETWEEN jobs — short-term search time that exists in every healthy economy; remedied by better information and matching

questions.question: STRUCTURAL unemployment is:
options: A MISMATCH between the skills or locations workers have and those employers need — South Africa's dominant type

questions.question: Cyclical unemployment is remedied by:
options: DEMAND — state spending, lower interest rates, export growth restoring the derived demand for labour

questions.question: The mineworker whose shaft closed and whose skills fit no growing sector is:
options: STRUCTURALLY unemployed — needing retraining and spatial remedies, not merely better adverts

questions.question: Structural and historical causes of SA unemployment include:
options: Capital-intensive mining and manufacturing, a skills pipeline misaligned with employer needs, and apartheid's spatial legacy

questions.question: For the ECONOMY, unemployment means:
options: Output forgone (producing inside the PPC), weaker aggregate demand, lost tax revenue as social spending needs rise, and decaying skills

questions.question: The self-reinforcing loop runs:
options: Unemployment raises spending, which raises production
Unemployment has no effect on production
Unemployment lowers spending → lower spending lowers production → lower production lowers hiring
Hiring falls only when wages rise

questions.question: For the INDIVIDUAL, unemployment is:
options: Only a temporary loss of wages
A statistical category with no personal effect
Lost income and poverty, grant and family dependence, eroded skills and confidence, with documented effects on health, dignity and family stability

questions.question: Growth of production creates jobs through:
options: DERIVED demand — more production requires more labour, especially where growth favours labour-intensive sectors

questions.question: Public works programmes are best judged as:
options: A permanent replacement for private employment
A BRIDGE, not a destination — immediate income, experience and assets, but temporary, budget-funded jobs that must lead onward
A cure for frictional unemployment only

questions.question: The UIF's crucial limitation is that it:
options: Only helps those who WERE formally employed — never the never-employed young person, South Africa's largest unemployed group

questions.question: The mature conclusion the examination wants:
options: DIAGNOSE before prescribing — cyclical needs demand, frictional needs information, structural needs education, training and spatial remedies, with works bridging and insurance cushioning

questions.question: "Experience is required to get the experience" describes:
options: The cruel loop facing first-time work-seekers, who are the front of every SA unemployment number
The frictional gap between school and work only

questions.question: The engineering firm with a three-person queue phoning agencies shows:
options: The SPLIT BY SKILL — same town, opposite problem: scarce skills short-queued, unskilled labour flooded

questions.question: The people who "stopped coming" to the queue:
options: Are counted in the strict rate
Left because they stopped believing the gate opens — invisible to the strict count, visible in the expanded one, and the deepest part of the problem

subtopics.title: Five Different Reasons for the Same Empty Hands

questions.question: The graduate who finished in November and starts in February is:
options: In the GAP — frictional unemployment, fixed by faster matching and information

questions.question: The matriculant in a town whose only vacancies demand "artisan, three years' experience" illustrates:
options: A MISMATCH — structural unemployment, needing training, trades and closing the distance between people and jobs

questions.question: The retrenchment letter arriving when orders dried up nationwide is:
options: CYCLICAL — it lifts when the economy lifts; the fix is demand

questions.question: "Anyone who offers one cure for all five stories is selling something" means:
options: DIAGNOSE BEFORE YOU PRESCRIBE — five causes need five different responses

questions.question: "Growing in what — and does it need people?" matters because:
options: A machine-heavy expansion can add billions in output and few jobs, while tourism, farming, construction and small business add far more hands per rand

questions.question: The honest limit of the public works BRIDGE is:
options: If the programme doesn't lead to a skill, certificate or next job, the bridge ends in the same river

questions.question: The NET (UIF) protects the economy as well as the worker because:
options: Benefits keep spending in the shops during downswings — stabilising the circular flow

questions.question: "A net with a hole where the young stand" means:
options: You can only claim from a job you HAD — the never-employed young person has paid nothing in and receives nothing out
